common_name: Early Amber Peach (Extra-Early Low-Chill Semi-Freestone Peach)

planting.note: Plant bare-root or containerized trees in late winter to early spring in full sun with excellent drainage; Early Amber needs only about 300-350 chill hours, so it sets fruit reliably in mild Gulf South and Deep South winters where higher-chill peaches often fail to bloom well.

directions: Plant bare-root or containerized trees in late winter to early spring in full sun with excellent drainage, and prune to an open-vase shape to admit light and air into the canopy. Early Amber is a very low-chill selection bred for mild-winter growing regions, requiring roughly 300-350 hours below 45 degrees F, which lets it flower and fruit consistently on the Gulf Coast even in warm winters that leave many standard peach cultivars barren. It is self-fruitful, so a single tree will produce a crop without a pollinator partner nearby, and it ripens extremely early, typically by late May in the Deep South. The medium-sized, semi-freestone fruit has yellow skin with a red blush and juicy, richly flavored yellow flesh; thin fruit to 6-8 inches apart when marble-sized to encourage larger, better-flavored peaches.

common_name: Ruby Sweet Plum (USDA Georgia-Bred Red-Fleshed Japanese Plum)

planting.note: Plant bare-root or container trees in late winter to early spring in well-drained, fertile soil in full sun; Ruby Sweet was released in 1989 by the USDA-ARS stone fruit breeding program in Byron, Georgia, the same program that produced Byrongold and Ruby Queen.

directions: Ruby Sweet resulted from a 1968 cross of Mariposa and Methley made by USDA breeder W.R. Okie at the Byron, Georgia research station, and was selected for markedly better flavor and disease tolerance than older Southeastern plums like Stanley. The fruit is medium to large with deep ruby-red skin and juicy red flesh, ripening in early-to-mid summer. It is not self-fruitful, so plant it alongside another Japanese plum such as Methley or Santa Rosa within pollinating range for reliable fruit set. Its chill requirement of roughly 400 hours runs toward the higher end for Gulf Coast zone 9a, so it is most reliable in the cooler pockets of the region and in years with a fuller winter chill; gardeners on the mildest coastal fringe should pair it with a very-low-chill variety as insurance.
